The region had to reinvent itself. This is called **structural change**. Today there are many universities, service firms and cultural attractions there.

Many old industrial buildings were not pulled down but converted into museums, concert venues or parks. The **Zollverein colliery** in Essen is part of the **UNESCO World Heritage**. In 2010 the Ruhr region was **European Capital of Culture**. Where winding towers once stood, people today walk on old spoil heaps.

gewusst: Because of its architecture, the Zollverein colliery is sometimes called the “most beautiful colliery in the world”.
Old heaps of rock from mining are often viewpoints with works of art in the Ruhr region today.

teile.einleitung: A state is a country with clear borders, a people who live there and a government of its own that rules over the country. On Earth there are just under 200 states, from huge ones such as Russia to tiny ones such as Vatican City. Switzerland too is a state, namely a federal state made up of 26 cantons.
wichtigste: A state needs a territory, a population and state authority.
The UN has 193 member states.
Russia is the largest country in the world by area.
Vatican City is the smallest country in the world.
Liechtenstein is a small neighbouring country to the east of Switzerland.
States can be republics or monarchies.
Switzerland has been a federal state since 1848.

abschnitte.text: According to a well-known theory of the lawyer Georg Jellinek, a state needs three things. The **territory** is the land within the borders. The **population** is the people who belong to it. The **state authority** is the power to make and enforce laws, for example through government, parliament, courts and police. If one of them is missing, people do not speak of a complete state.

**Russia**, with about 17 million square kilometres, is the largest country in the world and stretches across eleven time zones. Next come Canada, the USA and China. **Vatican City** in Rome is only about half a square kilometre in size and thus the smallest country. The Pope, the head of the Catholic Church, lives there. Monaco, San Marino and Liechtenstein are also among the microstates of Europe.

In a **republic** the head of state is elected, for example in France or Germany. In a **monarchy** a king, a queen or a prince is the head, and the office is mostly inherited. Examples are Great Britain, Spain and Liechtenstein. In a **democracy** the people have a say, whereas in a dictatorship one person or group rules alone.

Switzerland is a **federal state**: the Confederation, the 26 cantons and the communes share the tasks. Since 1848 it has had a common Federal Constitution. In direct democracy the citizens can often vote themselves. Since 2002 Switzerland has been a member of the UN, but not of the European Union.

Switzerland borders Germany, France, Italy, Austria and **Liechtenstein**. Liechtenstein lies in the east on the Rhine, is about 160 square kilometres in size and has Vaduz as its main town. It even uses the Swiss franc as its currency. States cooperate in organisations such as the **UN** to secure peace and solve shared problems.

begriffe.erklaerung: The land that lies within the borders of a state.
A state whose head is elected and not inherited.
A state with a king, a queen or a prince at its head.
A state made up of several member states, in Switzerland the cantons.
A state decides for itself and obeys no other state.

gewusst: Vatican City has a Swiss Guard of its own, which has protected the Pope for over 500 years.
Russia is so big that in one place it is already evening while in another the morning is only beginning.
Liechtenstein and Uzbekistan are the only doubly landlocked countries in the world: they are surrounded only by countries that themselves have no access to the sea.

teile.einleitung: Santiago de Chile is the capital and largest city of Chile. It lies in a wide valley behind which the high Andes rise. The River Mapocho flows through the city.
wichtigste: Santiago is the capital of Chile.
The city was founded in 1541 by Pedro de Valdivia.
The River Mapocho flows through Santiago.
In the east the snow-covered Andes rise.
A large part of the population of Chile lives in and around Santiago.
In the city there are often earthquakes.

abschnitte.titel: Founded at the hill of Santa Lucía
abschnitte.text: In 1541 the Spanish conqueror **Pedro de Valdivia** founded the city at the foot of the hill **Santa Lucía**. He named it after the apostle James, in Spanish Santiago. In the centre to this day lies the **Plaza de Armas** with the cathedral. Later Santiago became the capital of independent Chile.

abschnitte.titel: Between the Andes and the river
abschnitte.text: Santiago lies in a basin between the high **Andes** in the east and a lower coastal range in the west. Through the city flows the **Mapocho**, a river that comes from the Andes. From the hill **San Cristóbal** you have a wide view across the city to the mountains. In winter **smog** often lies over the valley, because the mountains hinder the exchange of air.

In and around Santiago live several million people, a large part of the whole population of Chile. The city has a modern **metro** and a business district with tower blocks. There stands the **Gran Torre Santiago**, one of the tallest buildings in South America. In the surrounding area many grapevines grow, because the climate is warm and dry in summer.

Chile lies where an oceanic plate dives beneath the South American Plate. That is why there are often **earthquakes** throughout the country and in Santiago too. New buildings are therefore built to be especially earthquake-proof. At school children regularly practise how they must behave in an earthquake.

gewusst: On clear days you can see from Santiago mountains of the Andes that are over 5,000 metres high.
In winter you can reach ski areas in the Andes from Santiago in a short time.

teile.einleitung: The Strait of Malacca is a long strait in South-East Asia. It lies between the Malay Peninsula and the island of Sumatra and is one of the busiest shipping routes in the world.
wichtigste: The Strait of Malacca lies between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra.
It connects the Indian Ocean with the Pacific.
It is about 900 kilometres long.
It is named after the port city of Malacca in Malaysia.
Portugal conquered Malacca in 1511.
Much oil from the Middle East sails through here to East Asia.

abschnitte.text: The **Strait of Malacca** lies between the **Malay Peninsula** and the Indonesian island of **Sumatra**. It connects the Andaman Sea in the **Indian Ocean** with the **South China Sea**, a marginal sea of the **Pacific**. From Singapore to the northern tip of Sumatra it is about **900 kilometres** long. At its narrowest point, the **Phillips Channel** near Singapore, the shipping channel is only about **2.8 kilometres** wide. This is one of the greatest bottlenecks of world shipping.

The strait is named after the port city of **Malacca** on the west coast of Malaysia. For centuries it was an important trading place for spices, silk and other goods. In **1511** the **Portuguese** under Afonso de Albuquerque conquered the city. Later the **Dutch** followed, and after them the **British**. In 2008 Malacca and **George Town** on the island of Penang were together included in the **UNESCO World Heritage**. Both show a mixture of Malay, Chinese, Indian and European culture.

abschnitte.titel: One of the most important sea routes
abschnitte.text: Every day very many ships sail through the strait: container ships, freighters and huge **tankers**. They carry, for example, **oil** from the Persian Gulf to China, Japan and South Korea, because this is the shortest sea route between these regions. Many goods from Asia that later end up in European shops also pass by here.

Because of the many ships and the narrow waters, raids by **pirates** were frequent, especially in the early 2000s. Joint **patrols** by the states bordering the strait have reduced the number of attacks. China depends heavily on the strait, because a large part of its oil imports sails through here. This worry is called the **Malacca dilemma**. The term became known in 2003 under President Hu Jintao.

gewusst: For many ships the Strait of Malacca is the shortest route between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific, which is why at its end lies Singapore, one of the largest ports in the world.
The old town of Malacca shows buildings from the Portuguese, Dutch and British periods side by side.

teile.einleitung: The red lionfish is a strikingly striped fish with long, poisonous spines. It actually comes from the Indian and Pacific Oceans, but today, as an introduced species, it threatens the coral reefs of the Caribbean.
wichtigste: The red lionfish has red and white stripes and long fin spines.
Its spines are poisonous and protect it from enemies.
Originally it lives in the Indo-Pacific and in the Red Sea.
It was introduced by humans to the Caribbean and the western Atlantic.
There it eats many small fish and has hardly any natural enemies.

abschnitte.text: The red lionfish stands out at once with its **red and white stripes** and its long, fan-like fins. In the fins sit **poisonous spines**. They protect it from enemies. For humans a sting is very painful. The red lionfish is a **predatory fish** and hunts smaller fish and crabs.

Originally the red lionfish lives in the **Indian** and **Pacific Oceans** and in the Red Sea. Probably some animals got into the sea from aquariums in Florida. Since then it has spread strongly in the **western Atlantic** and in the **Caribbean**. Such a species is called **invasive**. There it has hardly any **natural enemies**, because the local fish do not know it.

In the Caribbean the red lionfish eats very many small **reef fish**. Some of them keep the corals clean by eating algae. If they are missing, **algae** can overgrow the corals. That is why divers catch the fish on purpose. In some countries it is also offered as an **edible fish**, because its flesh is not poisonous.

gewusst: For some years the red lionfish has also been spreading in the Mediterranean.

teile.einleitung: Sian Ka'an is a large nature reserve on the Caribbean coast of the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico. It protects rainforest, mangroves, lagoons and part of a coral reef, and has been part of the UNESCO World Heritage since 1987.
wichtigste: Sian Ka'an lies in the Mexican state of Quintana Roo on the Caribbean.
It is a biosphere reserve, that is, a protected area for nature and people.
Since 1987 Sian Ka'an has been part of the UNESCO World Heritage.
There are rainforest, wetlands, lagoons, mangroves and coral reefs.
The name comes from the language of the Maya.

abschnitte.titel: A protected area by the sea
abschnitte.text: Sian Ka'an lies south of the town of **Tulum** in the state of **Quintana Roo**. The area is a **biosphere reserve**. This is the name for a protected area in which nature is preserved and people may nevertheless live and work gently. Because of its special landscape Sian Ka'an was included in the **UNESCO World Heritage** in 1987. The name comes from the language of the **Maya**, who lived here a long time ago.

In Sian Ka'an different landscapes meet. There are tropical **rainforest**, swamps and large **lagoons**. On the coast grow **mangroves**, trees that can stand in salt water. Off the coast lies part of a large **coral reef**. Many birds, fish and sea turtles live here, and in the forest also rare wild cats such as the jaguar.

Visitors can explore the area on boat trips through lagoons and canals. Because nature is sensitive, strict rules apply. Large hotels are not allowed there. In this way Sian Ka'an is meant to be preserved for animals and plants.

gewusst: In Sian Ka'an there are waterways that the Maya are said to have used a long time ago.

teile.einleitung: The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow strait between the Persian Gulf and the open sea. Huge tankers carrying oil sail through it. That is why it is one of the most important waterways in the world.
wichtigste: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman.
It connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea.
A large part of the oil from the Persian Gulf is shipped through it.
About a fifth of the oil used worldwide passes through this strait.
Tensions in the region often affect oil prices.

abschnitte.text: The **Strait of Hormuz** lies between **Iran** in the north and **Oman** in the south. It connects the **Persian Gulf** with the Gulf of Oman and on to the Arabian Sea. It is named after the small island of **Hormuz**. For ships that want to leave the Persian Gulf, there is no other sea route.

Around the Persian Gulf lie countries with very large **oil deposits**, such as Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kuwait, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and Iran. Their oil and natural gas is carried into the world by large **tankers**. About **a fifth** of the oil used worldwide is transported through the Strait of Hormuz. Much of it goes to Asia.

Because so much oil sails through the strait, it is politically very important. When **tensions** arise in the region, **oil prices** often rise all over the world. You can notice this in Switzerland too, for example in the prices of petrol and heating oil. Various states therefore protect shipping in this area.

gewusst: At its narrowest point the Strait of Hormuz is only a good 50 kilometres wide.
Some Gulf states have built pipelines so that part of their oil can bypass the strait.

teile.einleitung: Rio de Janeiro is one of the best-known cities in Brazil and in the whole world. It lies between mountains and the sea on a large bay and is famous for beaches, carnival and football.
wichtigste: Rio de Janeiro lies on Guanabara Bay on the Atlantic.
The name means “River of January” in English.
Until 1960 Rio was the capital of Brazil.
Well known are Sugarloaf Mountain with its cable car and Copacabana beach.
The famous football stadium is called Maracanã.
In 2016 the Summer Olympic Games took place here.
The people of Rio are called Cariocas.

abschnitte.text: Portuguese sailors reached the area in **January 1502**. They took the large bay for the mouth of a river. That is why they named the place **Rio de Janeiro**, in English **“River of January”**. In reality it is **Guanabara Bay**, a large sea bay on the **Atlantic**. Brazil became a colony of Portugal at the time, which is why Portuguese is spoken there.

In **1808** the **Portuguese royal court** fled from Napoleon’s troops to Rio de Janeiro. In this way the city became for some years the seat of the whole Portuguese empire. Later Rio was the **capital** of independent Brazil. In **1960** the government moved to the newly built city of **Brasília**. Since then Brasília has been the capital.

Rio lies between steep rocky mountains and the sea. The best-known rock is **Sugarloaf Mountain**, which a **cable car** goes up. On the mountain **Corcovado** stands the large statue of Christ, which looks out over the city. The most famous beach is called **Copacabana**. The beach of **Ipanema** is also known all over the world.

The **Maracanã** is one of the most famous football stadiums in the world. The deciding matches of the football World Cups of 1950 and 2014 took place there. Every year Rio celebrates **carnival** with big parades by the **samba schools**. In **2016** the **Summer Olympic Games** took place in Rio, the first in South America. The people of Rio are called **Cariocas**.

gewusst: The statue of Christ on Corcovado is one of the new seven wonders of the world.
The name Sugarloaf recalls the shape in which sugar was once sold.

teile.einleitung: In subsistence farming people produce mainly what they themselves need to live. They grow their own food and buy only little. This is how many small farming families in the world still live today.
wichtigste: Subsistence farming is production mainly for one’s own needs.
When surpluses are sold at local markets, it is called semi-subsistence farming.
According to the FAO, about 84 per cent of farms worldwide are smaller than two hectares.
Mixed cropping spreads the risk of crop failure.
Households without money and stores are especially at risk in a poor harvest.
South of the Sahara women do a large part of the field work.

abschnitte.text: In **subsistence farming** a household produces most of what it needs itself: grain, vegetables, milk or meat. **Money** and **markets** play only a small role. In the past many farming families in Switzerland also lived largely in this way. Today this form of economy is found mainly in poorer regions of Africa, Asia and Latin America.

Many small farmers live in a **semi-subsistence economy**. They cover their own needs first and then sell **surpluses** at local markets. With the money they pay for example school fees, tools or medicines. According to a **FAO** study of 2021, about **84 per cent** of all farms worldwide are smaller than **2 hectares**. But they farm only about 12 per cent of the agricultural land.

Subsistence farmers often rely on **mixed cropping** instead of monocultures. If one kind of plant fails because of drought or pests, the others still supply food. A famous example is the **milpa** in Mesoamerica: there **maize**, **beans** and **squash** grow together. The maize serves the beans as a climbing frame, the beans fix **nitrogen** in the soil, and the large squash leaves shade the ground. They are called the “three sisters”.

On many subsistence farms in Africa **cassava**, also called manioc, is a staple food. The plant originally comes from South America. It also grows on **poor soils** and withstands drought well. Its starchy **root tubers** can stay in the ground for a long time. In this way they serve as a store for difficult times.

Someone who has hardly any cash and stores cannot bridge a **drought** or a pest attack by buying food. A single bad harvest can then mean **hunger**. In many regions south of the Sahara **women** do a large part of the work: they work the fields, fetch water and process the harvest. Even so they often have fewer rights to land than men.

gewusst: Small farms under two hectares make up the largest part of all farms in the world, although they farm only a small part of the land.
Maize, beans and squash complement each other not only in the field, but also in the diet.

teile.einleitung: The concentric zone model is a well-known model from urban geography. It describes a city as a series of rings that lie around the centre, similar to the annual rings of a tree.
wichtigste: The sociologist Ernest W. Burgess published the concentric zone model in 1925.
The city of Chicago served as his example.
The classic model has five zones.
Directly around the business district lies the transition zone, and right on the outside the commuter zone.
The social status of the residents rises from the centre outwards.
The terms invasion and succession come from ecology.
Critics say the model overlooks transport routes and terrain.

abschnitte.text: The concentric zone model comes from the American sociologist **Ernest W. Burgess**. He published it in **1925**. Burgess did research together with **Robert E. Park** at the University of Chicago. Their line of research is called the **Chicago School**. The city of **Chicago** was growing very fast at the time and served Burgess as an example.

In the concentric zone model there are **five zones**. In the middle lies the **central business district** with offices and shops. Around it follows the **transition zone** with old houses, trades and many newcomers. After that comes the zone of **workers’ housing**, then a zone with better **residential houses**. The outermost ring is formed by the **commuter zone**. From there people travel every day to work in the city.

Burgess took over terms from **ecology**, the study of how living things exist together in nature. **Invasion** means that new groups move into an area. **Succession** means that they gradually replace the earlier residents. The growth of the city is driven by **immigration** and **population pressure**. Those who can afford it move further out. That is why the **social status** rises from the centre towards the edge.

The concentric zone model is very simplified. Critics say it overlooks **transport routes** such as roads and railway lines, and the **terrain**, such as rivers or hills. Real cities are rarely so round. That is why further models arose later, for example the **sector model** and the **multiple nuclei model**. In many European cities, too, wealthy families often live right in the centre, which contradicts the concentric zone model.

gewusst: The concentric zone model is still part of geography lessons in many countries today.
In the 19th century Chicago grew within a few decades into one of the largest cities in the USA.

teile.einleitung: The Rio Grande is one of the longest rivers in North America. For a large part of its course it forms the border between the USA and Mexico.
wichtigste: The name “Rio Grande” means “Big River” in Spanish.
In Mexico the river is called the Río Bravo.
It rises in the Rocky Mountains in the US state of Colorado.
It flows into the Gulf of Mexico.
Part of the river forms the border between the USA and Mexico.
El Paso and Ciudad Juárez face each other across the river.
Big Bend National Park in Texas lies on a large bend of the river.

abschnitte.titel: From the mountains to the sea
abschnitte.text: The Rio Grande **rises** in the **Rocky Mountains** in the state of **Colorado**. From there it flows south through **New Mexico**. After that it flows south-east and forms the border between the US state of **Texas** and **Mexico**. It is about 3,000 kilometres long. Finally it **flows into** the **Gulf of Mexico**.

**Rio Grande** is Spanish and means **“Big River”**. That is what it is called in the USA. In **Mexico**, by contrast, it is called the **Río Bravo**, often also Río Bravo del Norte. “Bravo” here means something like wild or fierce. The Spanish names date from the time when Spain ruled large parts of this region.

From the city of **El Paso** the river forms the border between the **USA** and **Mexico**. Directly opposite El Paso lies the Mexican city of **Ciudad Juárez**. Such cities are called **twin cities**. Many bridges connect the two banks. The border along the river is often discussed politically in both countries.

In Texas the river makes a large bend, called **Big Bend** in English. There lies **Big Bend National Park** with deep gorges and desert landscape. The Rio Grande flows through very dry regions. A lot of water is diverted for fields and cities. That is why in some places it carries only little water or even dries up for a time.

gewusst: In Mexico and the USA the same river has two different names.
The Rio Grande is one of the longest rivers in North America.

teile.einleitung: A smart city is a city that uses digital technology and data to run its operations. Sensors and networking are meant to make traffic flow better, save energy and make life more pleasant. At the same time there are concerns about data protection and surveillance.
wichtigste: A smart city controls processes such as traffic, energy or waste with data and digital technology.
The aims are more efficiency, sustainability and quality of life.
Songdo in South Korea and Masdar City near Abu Dhabi were built as planned cities.
Since 2014 Singapore has pursued the “Smart Nation” initiative.
A digital twin is a virtual copy of a city.
Common points of criticism are surveillance and a lack of data protection.

abschnitte.text: In a **smart city**, **sensors** measure, for example, how many cars drive along a street, how full a bin is or how much electricity is used. The data are collected and analysed over the internet. In this way traffic lights can steer traffic better, or street lamps can shine only when someone comes past. The aims are more **efficiency**, **sustainability** and **quality of life**.

Some cities were planned as smart cities from the start. **Songdo** near Incheon in South Korea was built from the 2000s on reclaimed land. Critics find that the city feels hardly lively despite its technology. **Masdar City** near Abu Dhabi was meant from 2008 to become a city with renewable energy and little car traffic. The original aims were scaled back several times, though.

The city-state of **Singapore** started the **“Smart Nation”** initiative in 2014. It relies on sensors, digital public services and data-based traffic control. In rankings Singapore is often regarded as the leader. In **Toronto** the firm **Sidewalk Labs**, a subsidiary of Alphabet, wanted to build a data-driven district called **Quayside**. After criticism of data protection and because of the pandemic, the project was abandoned in 2020.

A **digital twin** is a virtual copy of a city with buildings, streets and pipes. With it you can test plans on a computer before you build. Cities such as **Zurich** use 3D city models as the basis for this. A **smart grid** is an intelligent electricity network. It matches generation and consumption to each other with the help of data. In this way fluctuating energy sources such as sun and wind can be integrated better.

Smart cities collect large amounts of data about the movements and behaviour of people. Critics warn of **surveillance** and a lack of **data protection**. They also ask who owns the data and how much power private technology firms get. Supporters stress the benefit for the environment and daily life. Many cities try to weigh up both and let the population have a say.

gewusst: Some smart cities have street lamps that only get brighter when someone walks past.
Songdo in South Korea was built on land that used to be sea.

teile.einleitung: The South Island is the largest island of New Zealand. It is known for high mountains, glaciers, deep fjords and adventure sports.
wichtigste: The South Island is the larger of the two main islands of New Zealand.
Cook Strait separates it from the North Island.
Through the island run the Southern Alps with Aoraki/Mount Cook.
Christchurch is the largest city and was hit by a severe earthquake in 2011.
Milford Sound is a famous fjord in the south-west.

abschnitte.text: Along the island run the **Southern Alps**. Their highest peak is **Aoraki/Mount Cook**, the highest mountain in New Zealand. On the rainy west coast the **Franz Josef Glacier** and the **Fox Glacier** reach down almost to the rainforest. This is very rare in the world. The South Island is more than three times as big as Switzerland, but has far fewer inhabitants than the North Island.

In the south-west lies **Fiordland National Park**. There glaciers ground out deep valleys in the Ice Age, which are filled with sea water today. The most famous fjord is called **Milford Sound**. Steep rock walls rise out of the water, and after rain many waterfalls plunge down. Sometimes you can see dolphins and seals.

**Christchurch** is the largest city of the South Island. In **2011** it was hit by a severe **earthquake**. Many buildings collapsed, and the well-known cathedral was also badly damaged. New Zealand lies on the boundary of two tectonic plates, which is why the ground often shakes there. Since then the city has been largely rebuilt.

**Queenstown** lies on **Lake Wakatipu** and is surrounded by mountains. The town is famous for **bungee jumping**, jet boat rides and skiing. Near Queenstown one of the first commercial bungee sites in the world was set up in the late 1980s. For films such as “The Lord of the Rings” too, many scenes were shot on the South Island.

gewusst: On the South Island lives the kea, one of the few parrots that live in the mountains in snow.
In Māori the South Island is called Te Waipounamu.

teile.einleitung: Salt weathering is a form of weathering in which salt breaks rock into pieces. Growing salt crystals press so strongly in fine cracks and pores that the rock crumbles. This happens in nature, but also on houses and bridges.
wichtigste: In salt weathering the pressure of growing salt crystals destroys the rock.
It is a kind of physical weathering.
It is especially common in dry regions and on sea coasts.
It often produces honeycomb-like holes called tafoni.
Road salt can cause flaking on buildings and bridges.
White crusts of salt on damp walls are called efflorescence.

abschnitte.text: Water containing salt penetrates tiny **pores** and **cracks** in the rock. When the water evaporates, the salt is left behind and forms **crystals**. These crystals go on growing when new salt water arrives. As they do so, they press against the walls of the pores. After many repetitions grains and small pieces come loose from the stone. Because only forces are at work and the rock is not changed chemically, this counts as **physical weathering**.

Salt weathering is common in **dry regions**. There water evaporates quickly, and there is often a lot of salt in the ground. It also plays a large part on **sea coasts**, because the spray constantly splashes salt water onto the rocks. In deserts it often works together with **insolation weathering**: the sun heats the stone strongly, the water evaporates faster, and the crystals grow more quickly.

Salt weathering often produces round hollows in rock faces, which are called **tafoni**. Sometimes many small holes lie close together, which looks like a honeycomb. This is then called **honeycomb weathering**. Such forms are found, for example, on sandstone cliffs on coasts in the Mediterranean region.

Houses, walls and bridges also suffer from salt. In winter **road salt** is spread on many Swiss roads. The salty meltwater splashes onto bridge piers and house walls. There the crystals grow and **flaking** occurs. On damp walls white crusts often form, called **efflorescence**. That is why buildings are protected with coatings and good drainage.

gewusst: On old monuments and statues made of stone, too, salt is one of the greatest enemies.
Efflorescence on cellar walls often shows that damp is getting into the masonry.

teile.einleitung: Infant mortality states how many children die before their first birthday. It is an important figure for comparing living conditions in a country.
wichtigste: The deaths in the first year of life are counted per 1,000 live births.
In Switzerland the figure is about 3 per 1,000.
Worldwide, according to the UN, it was about 27 per 1,000 around 2023.
Neonatal mortality counts only the first 28 days of life.
Vaccinations, clean water and good nutrition reduce the figure greatly.
The figure is highest in Africa south of the Sahara.

abschnitte.text: Infant mortality counts the children who die in the **first year of life**. It is always converted to **1,000 live births**, so that countries can be compared. An example: in a country 50,000 children are born alive, and 1,500 die in the first year. 1,500 divided by 50,000 gives 0.03, times 1,000 is **30 per 1,000**. **Neonatal mortality** counts only the first 28 days, in which the risk is greatest.

Infants are very vulnerable. Bad drinking water, too little food and a lack of doctors hit them first. That is why infant mortality is regarded as an important **development indicator**, that is, a measure of the state of a country. It shows how good **health care, hygiene and nutrition** are. It is highest in **Africa south of the Sahara**, for example in Niger or Somalia.

Around 1900 well over 100 out of 1,000 infants in Switzerland still died. Today it is **about 3 per 1,000**, one of the lowest figures in the world. Worldwide, too, the figure has fallen sharply. According to the UN it was about **27 per 1,000** around 2023; in 1990 it was still more than twice as high.

In the 20th century **vaccinations** against measles, diphtheria or whooping cough protected very many children. Clean water and good hygiene are just as important. For diarrhoea a simple **oral rehydration solution** of water, salt and sugar helps. It replaces the lost fluid, is cheap and has saved the lives of millions of children.

Researchers have observed a connection. When infant mortality falls, the **birth rate** usually falls later too. Parents who can be sure that their children will survive often want fewer children. This change is called the **demographic transition**.

gewusst: The solution of water, salt and sugar costs only a few Rappen and is regarded as one of the greatest advances in medicine.
The world’s infant mortality has more than halved since 1990.

teile.einleitung: A satellite image is a photograph of the Earth taken from space. Satellites orbit the Earth and look down on it with cameras. In this way we see clouds, seas, deserts and cities from above.
wichtigste: A satellite image is a photograph of the Earth from space.
For this, satellites need a camera or other measuring instruments.
In the pictures clouds and ice are white, forests green and the Sahara yellowish brown.
Weather satellites help with weather forecasting.
At night you can see the lights of the cities.
In winter you can clearly see the white Alps in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: A **satellite** is a device that orbits the Earth. Many satellites carry a **camera** or other measuring instruments. They take pictures of the Earth and send them by radio to antennas on the ground. Some satellites can even measure heat or light that our eyes cannot see. Astronauts also take photographs of the Earth from the **ISS** space station. The ISS orbits the Earth about **15 times a day**.

On satellite images you recognise the Earth by its colours. **Clouds** and **ice** are white, the seas dark blue. Large **forests** appear green, the **Sahara** yellowish brown. In winter on pictures of Switzerland you clearly see the **white Alps**, while the Swiss Plateau is often green or lies under fog. At night the **lights of the cities** glow, especially well in Europe.

**Weather satellites** observe how clouds and storms move. Some of them stand apparently motionless over one point of the Earth at a height of about 36,000 kilometres. In this way they always see the same area and can take a new picture every few minutes. Weather services, including MeteoSwiss, use these pictures for the **weather forecast**.

Satellite images help to draw **maps** and to recognise changes. You can see, for example, how glaciers melt, forests are cleared or cities grow. After floods or earthquakes they show rescuers where help is needed. The map programs on your mobile phone also use satellite images.

The first Swiss person in space was **Claude Nicollier**. In 1992 he flew into space for the first time in an American Space Shuttle. In all he was in space four times. On several flights he helped to repair and improve the **Hubble** space telescope.

gewusst: The ISS flies so fast that the astronauts experience about 15 sunrises in a day.
The first satellite images of the Earth were taken more than 60 years ago.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland is a small country in the middle of Europe, known for its mountains, lakes, four national languages and direct democracy. It borders Germany, France, Italy, Austria and Liechtenstein. In Switzerland people pay with the Swiss franc.
wichtigste: In Switzerland people pay with francs and Rappen.
Switzerland consists of 26 cantons.
Bern is the federal city, where the government and parliament sit.
The four national languages are German, French, Italian and Romansh.
About 9 million people live in Switzerland (as of 2024).
Switzerland is neutral and not a member of the European Union.
The highest mountain is the Dufourspitze in the Monte Rosa massif at 4,634 metres.

abschnitte.text: Switzerland is about 41,000 square kilometres in size and has no access to the sea. It is divided into three landscapes: the **Jura** in the north-west, the **Swiss Plateau** in the middle and the **Alps** in the south, which cover more than half of the area. On the Swiss Plateau lie most of the towns, fields and roads. Because of its many rivers and glaciers, Switzerland is also called the water tower of Europe.

According to tradition, in 1291 the valley communities of Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden joined together in a league, which is why the national holiday is celebrated on 1 August. In the course of the centuries further places joined. In 1848 Switzerland became a **federal state** with a common constitution. Since 2002 Switzerland has been a member of the UN.

Switzerland is a **direct democracy**: the people can vote several times a year on laws and changes to the constitution. The government, the Federal Council, consists of seven members. The parliament in Bern has two chambers, the National Council and the Council of States. The cantons and communes have many tasks of their own, for example the schools.

The currency is the **Swiss franc**, abbreviated CHF, and one franc has 100 Rappen. The Swiss National Bank issues the money. Important for the economy are banks and insurance companies, the pharmaceutical industry, machinery and watches. Swiss chocolate and cheese are also known all over the world.

In Switzerland four national languages are spoken. German, mostly as Swiss German in everyday life, is spoken by most people, French in **Romandie** in the west, Italian in Ticino and in parts of the Grisons. **Romansh** is spoken only in the Grisons. About a quarter of the population does not have a Swiss passport, so many other languages are heard too.

Switzerland has long been **neutral** and takes no part in the wars of other countries. In Geneva many international organisations have their headquarters, such as the Red Cross, which was founded there in 1863, and a major seat of the UN. Switzerland is not in the EU, but has many treaties with it. Every year millions of tourists visit places such as the Matterhorn, the Jungfrau or Lucerne.

begriffe.erklaerung: One of the 26 member states of Switzerland, with its own government.
The seat of government and parliament; in Switzerland that is Bern.
The people themselves decide important questions in votes.
A state takes no side in the wars of other countries.

gewusst: Switzerland has no official capital; Bern is called the federal city.
On Swiss coins stands the Latin name “Helvetia” and not “Switzerland”.
Besides that of the Vatican, the Swiss flag is one of the two square national flags.

teile.einleitung: The South China Sea is a large marginal sea of the Pacific Ocean in South-East Asia. It is an important sea route and at the same time an area over which several states are in dispute.
wichtigste: The South China Sea belongs to the Pacific Ocean.
It lies between southern China, Vietnam, the Philippines and Borneo.
The Strait of Malacca connects it with the Indian Ocean.
Several states lay claim to the Spratly Islands.
Singapore and Hong Kong lie on this sea.

abschnitte.titel: A marginal sea of the Pacific
abschnitte.text: The South China Sea is a **marginal sea of the western Pacific**. It lies between **southern China**, **Vietnam**, the **Philippines**, **Malaysia** and the island of **Borneo**. Taiwan, Brunei and Indonesia also border on it. **Japan**, by contrast, lies further north on the East China Sea. In summer and autumn strong tropical storms, the **typhoons**, often pass over the sea.

Every day very many ships sail through the South China Sea. They carry goods back and forth between East Asia, Europe and the Middle East. The **Strait of Malacca** between Malaysia and the island of Sumatra connects the sea with the **Indian Ocean**. It is one of the busiest shipping routes in the world.

In the sea lie many small islands and reefs, for example the **Spratly Islands** and the Paracel Islands. Several states make claims to them, among them **China**, **Vietnam** and the **Philippines**. It is about fishing grounds, possible resources such as oil, and control of the sea routes. China has piled up artificial islands on some reefs, which other states criticise. The dispute is still unresolved to this day.

At the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula lies **Singapore**. Its port is one of the largest in the world. At the mouth of the Pearl River lies **Hong Kong**, a **special administrative region** of China with its own law and its own currency. The great river **Mekong** also flows into the South China Sea.

gewusst: A large part of world trade at sea sails through the South China Sea.
In the sea there are large coral reefs with very many species of fish.

teile.einleitung: Sri Lanka is an island country in the Indian Ocean, south of India. The island is known for its tea, old royal cities and Buddhist temples. Until 1972 the country was called Ceylon.
wichtigste: Until 1972 Sri Lanka was called Ceylon.
The country is famous for its tea, Ceylon tea.
The Palk Strait separates Sri Lanka from India.
Colombo is the largest city, and the capital is Sri Jayewardenepura Kotte.
Most people are Buddhists.
The rock fortress of Sigiriya and the Temple of the Tooth in Kandy are famous places.

abschnitte.text: Sri Lanka lies in the **Indian Ocean**, south of the tip of India. Between southern India and the north of Sri Lanka lies the **Palk Strait**. At its narrowest point this strait is only about 50 kilometres wide. The largest city and economic centre is **Colombo**. The official capital is the neighbouring **Sri Jayewardenepura Kotte**.

For a long time the island was under the rule of European powers, last of all the **British**. At that time it was called **Ceylon**. In 1948 the country became independent. In **1972** it took the name **Sri Lanka**. The name Ceylon lives on, though, in the famous **Ceylon tea**.

Sri Lanka is one of the largest **tea producers** in the world. The British laid out large **tea plantations** in the highlands. There the tea bushes grow on steep, green slopes. The leaves are picked by hand. To this day the tea is sold all over the world as **Ceylon tea**, including to Switzerland.

About two thirds of the people in Sri Lanka are **Buddhists**. In addition there are **Hindus**, **Muslims** and **Christians**. In the city of **Kandy** stands the famous **Temple of the Tooth**. There a tooth of the Buddha is revered as a **relic**. Every year a great festival with decorated **elephants** takes place in honour of the relic.

In the middle of the country a rock about 180 metres high rises up: **Sigiriya**, the “Lion Rock”. In the 5th century **King Kassapa** used it as a palace and fortress. On the rock old **wall paintings** have been preserved. Today Sigiriya is a **World Heritage Site** and attracts many visitors.

gewusst: Even after the new name Sri Lanka, the island’s tea is still called Ceylon tea.
At the entrance to Sigiriya you can still see huge stone lion paws.

teile.einleitung: Gentle tourism is a way of travelling in which nature, landscape and local people are spared as far as possible. Visitors are meant to enjoy an area without harming it. In the Alps especially this is an important subject.
wichtigste: Gentle tourism means travel that spares nature and local people as far as possible.
Instead of by car, people often travel by train, bus, bicycle or on foot.
Local products, accommodation and offers are used.
The idea arose in the 1970s and 1980s.
In Switzerland there are several car-free holiday resorts.

abschnitte.text: In **gentle tourism** travellers are meant to get to know an area without burdening it. Nature is to stay protected, and local people are to benefit from tourism. The opposite is often called **hard tourism** or **mass tourism**: large hotel complexes, a lot of traffic and visitors who stay only briefly. The idea arose in the 1970s and 1980s, when many holiday resorts were being built up more and more.

Those who travel gently go on holiday, for example, by **train** or **bus** instead of by car or aeroplane. On the spot they get around on foot, by bicycle or by public transport. They stay in small hotels or on farms and eat **local products**. They keep to the paths, leave no rubbish behind and respect the customs of the people.

In Switzerland there are several **car-free holiday resorts**, for example **Zermatt**, **Saas-Fee**, **Wengen**, **Mürren** and **Braunwald**. They can be reached by train, cable car or PostBus. Many places offer guest cards with which you can use buses and trains cheaply. The Swiss tourism researcher **Jost Krippendorf** warned as early as the 1970s that too much building destroys the landscape.

Gentle tourism is often more expensive or more demanding than a package holiday. Some places, however, live precisely from many visitors. That is why communities look for a middle way between income and protection of nature. The visitors themselves, too, can achieve a great deal with their decisions.

gewusst: In Zermatt no ordinary cars run, only small electric vehicles.
The term “gentle travel” was made known around 1980 by the futurologist Robert Jungk.

teile.einleitung: With language people communicate with one another: they speak, listen, write and read. In the world there are about 7,000 different languages. In Switzerland too there are several national languages.
wichtigste: In the world there are about 7,000 languages.
Chinese is the most common mother tongue in the world.
English is learned by the most people as a foreign language.
Arabic is written from right to left.
In Chinese, characters are used instead of letters.
Switzerland has four national languages, and Romansh is spoken mainly in Graubünden.

abschnitte.text: Researchers count about **7,000 languages** in the world. Some are spoken by millions of people, others by only a few. The language you learn first as a child is called your **mother tongue**. Most people have **Chinese**, above all Mandarin, as their mother tongue. This is because very many people live in China.

A language that you learn in addition is called a **foreign language**. The most people learn **English** as a foreign language. It is taught at school in many countries. Pilots and air traffic controllers also speak English with each other so that everyone understands. Someone who speaks several languages is called **multilingual**.

Languages are written in very different ways. We write German with letters from left to right. **Arabic**, by contrast, is written from **right to left**. In **Chinese** there are no letters, but thousands of **characters**. One character often stands for a whole word or a syllable.

In many countries more than one language is spoken. In **Belgium** people speak **Dutch** in the north and **French** in the south, and in the east there is also a small German-speaking area. In **Canada** people speak English and French. In the province of **Quebec** most people speak French. In **Austria** people speak German, but with words of their own, for example “Paradeiser” for tomato.

Switzerland has **four national languages**: German, French, Italian and **Romansh**. German is spoken in German-speaking Switzerland, French in the Romandie and Italian mainly in Ticino. Romansh is the smallest national language. It is spoken mainly in the canton of **Graubünden**. In German-speaking Switzerland people mostly speak **dialect** in everyday life, that is, Swiss German.

gewusst: Many of the about 7,000 languages of the world are spoken by only a few people.
On every Swiss banknote there are texts in all four national languages.

teile.einleitung: In subduction one tectonic plate dives beneath another and sinks into the Earth’s mantle. This process forms deep-sea trenches and chains of volcanoes and triggers the strongest earthquakes in the world.
wichtigste: In subduction an oceanic plate dives beneath another plate.
Oceanic plates are denser and heavier than continental ones.
At subduction zones the strongest earthquakes occur, the megathrust earthquakes.
Subduction earthquakes often trigger tsunamis.
When two continents collide, a fold mountain range is piled up.
The slab pull of the sinking plate drives the movement of the plates.

abschnitte.text: The Earth’s surface consists of large **plates** that move slowly. When an **oceanic** and a **continental** plate collide, the oceanic one dives down. The reason is that oceanic lithosphere of **basalt** is **denser** and heavier than continental crust. It sinks into the **Earth’s mantle**. This process is called **subduction**. Where the plate dives down, a deep **deep-sea trench** often forms.

As it dives, sediments are scraped off the lower plate and attached to the upper plate. In this way an **accretionary wedge** grows. At depth cool rock quickly comes under high pressure, but stays relatively cold. This produces a special metamorphic rock, **blueschist**. It is named after the bluish mineral **glaucophane**.

At the boundary between the plates the rocks catch on each other. Over centuries **tension** builds up. When it is suddenly released, the strongest quakes on Earth occur, the **megathrust earthquakes**. The upper plate, which has been bent over the years, snaps back and lifts the **sea floor** with a jolt. This displaces the whole column of water above it and triggers a **tsunami**.

On the north-west coast of America lies the **Cascadia** subduction zone. When the last great quake took place there was found out in an astonishing way. In **Japan** a tsunami was recorded in January 1700 without the ground having shaken there. Together with dead forests on the coast of North America, the quake could be dated to **26 January 1700**.

The cold, heavy plate sinks into the mantle and pulls the rest of the plate along behind it. This **slab pull** is regarded as one of the strongest driving forces of plate movement. When two **continental** plates collide, by contrast, neither can dive deep, because continental crust is too light. The plates are squeezed together and pile up a **fold mountain range**, such as the **Himalaya**. The Alps too came about through the collision of plates.

gewusst: Around the Pacific there are so many subduction zones with volcanoes that people speak of the “Pacific Ring of Fire”.
The Cascadia earthquake of 1700 could be dated to the exact day, although at that time there were no written records of it in North America.

teile.einleitung: A tourist attraction is a place or a building that is so special that people travel from far away to see it. It can be an ancient tomb, a giant statue, a city of rock or a modern building. Some attractions are so famous that almost every child recognises them in a photograph.
wichtigste: Attractions can be built by people or created by nature.
The Taj Mahal in India was built as a tomb.
The great statue of Christ on Mount Corcovado stands in Rio de Janeiro.
The rock city of Petra lies in Jordan.
France gave the USA the Statue of Liberty in New York.
The opera house with the sail-shaped roofs stands in Sydney harbour.
UNESCO includes especially valuable places in the World Heritage.

abschnitte.text: The **Taj Mahal** stands in the city of Agra in the north of India. The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan had it built in the 17th century as a **tomb** for his late wife Mumtaz Mahal. The building is of white marble and decorated with precious stones. Depending on the time of day it shimmers white, pink or golden. Every year millions of people visit this place.

The **statue of Christ** on Mount Corcovado looks out over the city of Rio de Janeiro in Brazil. It was completed in 1931 and is about 30 metres high, with its pedestal even about 38 metres. The **rock city of Petra** in Jordan was built about 2,000 years ago by the Nabataean people. Its temples and tombs were cut directly out of reddish sandstone. Famous above all is the Treasury, which you reach through a narrow gorge.

abschnitte.titel: Statue of Liberty and opera house
abschnitte.text: The **Statue of Liberty** stands on a small island off New York. France gave it to the USA, and it was inaugurated in 1886. The framework inside was designed by Gustave Eiffel, who later also built the Eiffel Tower in Paris. The **Sydney Opera House** in Australia was designed by the Danish architect Jørn Utzon and opened in 1973. Its white roofs recall sails in the wind.

**UNESCO** is an organisation of the United Nations for education, science and culture. It keeps a list of the **World Heritage** of humankind. On it are over 1,000 especially valuable places all over the world. The countries undertake to protect these places and to preserve them for later generations.

Switzerland too has many attractions. The World Heritage includes, for example, the **old town of Bern**, the Abbey of St Gallen, the castles of Bellinzona and the Rhaetian Railway over the Albula and the Bernina. World famous too are the **Matterhorn** near Zermatt, the Chapel Bridge in Lucerne and the Rhine Falls near Schaffhausen. Every year they attract many visitors from all over the world.

When very many people visit a place at the same time, it is called **mass tourism**. Then there are long queues, rubbish and sometimes damage to old buildings. That is why some places sell only a limited number of tickets. As a visitor you should not touch anything that is protected, and should not leave any rubbish behind.

begriffe.erklaerung: A building in which a dead person is buried and remembered.
An organisation of the UN that looks after education, science and culture.
Places that are so valuable to all humankind that they are given special protection.
Travelling in your free time to get to know other places.
A person who plans and designs buildings.

gewusst: The Statue of Liberty was originally copper brown; through wind and weather it turned green in time.
In Petra scenes of the film “Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade” were shot.
The statue of Christ in Rio is struck by lightning from time to time.

teile.einleitung: Dew is made of fine drops of water that form on grass, leaves and cars in the morning. It does not fall from the sky but forms directly on cold surfaces.
wichtigste: Dew forms directly on grass and other surfaces.
It forms when the air cools down during the night.
Water vapour from the air then condenses into drops.
Dew is a deposited form of precipitation.
If it is colder than zero degrees, frost forms instead of dew.

abschnitte.text: There is always invisible **water vapour** in the air. Cold air can hold less water vapour than warm air. On clear nights, grass, leaves and car roofs cool down strongly. When the air at these surfaces gets so cold that it can no longer hold the vapour, the vapour **condenses** into tiny drops. The temperature at which this happens is called the **dew point**.

abschnitte.titel: When there is a lot of dew
abschnitte.text: Most dew forms on **clear, windless nights**. Without clouds, the heat of the ground can radiate well into the sky. Clouds, on the other hand, act like a blanket and hold the warmth back. Wind mixes the air, so less dew forms when it is windy. In the morning the sun makes the drops **evaporate** again.

Rain, snow and hail fall from the sky. Dew, on the other hand, forms **right at the ground**. That is why it is called a **deposited form of precipitation**. If it is colder than zero degrees at night, fine ice crystals form instead of drops. This is **frost**, which covers meadows and trees in white.

Spiders' webs covered with dew glitter in the morning like strings of pearls. You can see the same process when a glass of cold water becomes wet on the outside. In very dry regions, dew is an important source of water for some plants and small animals.

gewusst: On meadows so much dew can form in one night that your shoes get completely wet as you walk.
Car windows are also often covered in dew in the morning, because they cool down quickly during the night.

teile.einleitung: An ice shelf is a huge plate of ice that floats on the sea but is still connected to the land. It forms from glaciers that flow from the land into the sea. Most ice shelves are found around Antarctica.
wichtigste: An ice shelf is a plate of ice that floats on the sea.
The ice comes from glaciers on the land.
Most ice shelves lie in Antarctica.
The largest is the Ross Ice Shelf, about as big as France.
The second largest is the Filchner-Ronne Ice Shelf.
The Larsen B ice shelf broke up within a few weeks in 2002.

abschnitte.titel: Ice that floats on the sea
abschnitte.text: In Antarctica huge **glaciers** flow slowly from the land into the sea. There they do not stop, but push out onto the water as a thick plate. This floating plate is called an **ice shelf**. It is usually **several hundred metres thick**. Because ice is lighter than water, it floats, but it stays frozen fast to the land.

Most ice shelves are found around **Antarctica**, with smaller areas in Greenland and the north of Canada too. The largest in the world is the **Ross Ice Shelf**. It is about as big as **France**. The second largest is the **Filchner-Ronne Ice Shelf** on the Weddell Sea. Together the ice shelves of Antarctica cover a huge area of sea.

abschnitte.titel: High walls of ice and icebergs
abschnitte.text: At the edge facing the open sea the ice shelf often forms a **high wall of ice** that rises steeply out of the water. Pieces keep breaking off there, which is called **calving**. In this way **tabular icebergs** form, which are flat like a table. Some of them are huge, even **bigger than the canton of Zurich**. They can drift for years through the Southern Ocean.

abschnitte.titel: When an ice shelf breaks up
abschnitte.text: In 2002 the **Larsen B** ice shelf on the Antarctic Peninsula broke up within a few weeks. It had already been getting thinner before that, because the air and the sea there were getting warmer. An ice shelf acts like a **brake** on the glaciers behind it. If it is missing, the glaciers flow faster into the sea, and the **sea level** rises. That is why researchers observe ice shelves closely with satellites.

gewusst: When floating ice shelf melts, the sea level hardly rises, much as a melting ice cube does not make a glass overflow.
Under some ice shelves fish and other animals live in complete darkness.

teile.einleitung: Roald Amundsen was a Norwegian polar explorer. In 1911 he was the first to reach the South Pole, and he is among the most famous explorers in history.
wichtigste: Amundsen first studied medicine, at his mother’s wish.
From 1903 to 1906 he was the first to sail through the whole of the Northwest Passage.
In 1910 he sailed with the ship Fram towards Antarctica.
On 14 December 1911 five men stood with him at the South Pole.
Dogs pulled the sledges of his expedition.
In 1926 he flew over the North Pole in the airship Norge.
In 1928 he lost his life on a rescue flight in the Arctic.

abschnitte.text: Roald Amundsen was born in 1872 in **Norway**. At his mother’s wish he began **studying medicine**. But even as a young man he dreamed of journeys into the eternal ice. After his mother’s death he gave up his studies and went to sea. He took part in an expedition to Antarctica and learned a great deal there about life in the cold.

The **Northwest Passage** is a sea route through the Arctic Ocean in the north of America. It connects the Atlantic with the Pacific. Many seafarers had tried in vain to sail through it. From **1903 to 1906** Amundsen was the first to succeed completely, with the small ship **Gjøa**. On the way he learned from the **Inuit** how to dress in the Arctic and how to travel with dogs.

In **1910** Amundsen sailed with the ship **Fram** towards **Antarctica**. At the same time the Briton Robert Falcon Scott was on his way to the South Pole. Amundsen relied on **sledge dogs** and on good skiers. On **14 December 1911** he reached the **South Pole** with four companions. So there were **five** of them, and they all returned safely.

abschnitte.titel: Over the North Pole by airship
abschnitte.text: Later Amundsen wanted to explore the Arctic from the air. In **1926** he flew over the **North Pole** in the **airship Norge**. On board with him were the Italian Umberto Nobile and the American Lincoln Ellsworth. In **1928** Nobile crashed in another airship in the Arctic. Amundsen flew off to help with the **rescue**, and never came back.

gewusst: The research station at the South Pole is called the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station, after the two polar explorers.
The Fram, in which Amundsen sailed to Antarctica, stands today in a museum in Oslo.

teile.einleitung: With the Saffir-Simpson hurricane wind scale, hurricanes are divided into five categories according to their wind speed. In this way you quickly know how dangerous a storm is.
wichtigste: The Saffir-Simpson scale divides hurricanes into five categories.
What counts is the sustained wind speed.
Category 1 begins at about 119 km/h, category 5 at about 252 km/h.
From category 3 it is called a major hurricane.
The scale is named after Herbert Saffir and Robert Simpson.

abschnitte.text: The scale was developed in the USA in the early 1970s. It is named after the civil engineer **Herbert Saffir** and the meteorologist **Robert Simpson**. Simpson was then the head of the **National Hurricane Center** of the USA. A **hurricane** is a strong cyclone over the Atlantic or the eastern Pacific. In the western Pacific such storms are called **typhoons**.

The scale has **five categories**. What is decisive is the **sustained wind speed**. **Category 1** begins at about **119 km/h** and can, for example, break off branches and damage roofs. With each category the danger rises. **Category 5** begins at about **252 km/h** and can destroy houses completely. From **category 3** it is called a **major hurricane**.

abschnitte.titel: What the scale does not show
abschnitte.text: The scale measures only the **wind**. In a hurricane, however, **storm surges**, in which the sea pushes far inland, and heavy **rain** are also dangerous. That is why even a category 1 storm can cause great floods. Weather services therefore warn not only with the category, but also about water and rain.

gewusst: Hurricanes are given names, which according to fixed lists are given alternately to women and men.

teile.einleitung: The Sistema Ox Bel Ha is a huge network of caves filled with water. It lies underground near Tulum on the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico and is regarded as the longest explored underwater cave system in the world (as of 2026).
wichtigste: Ox Bel Ha lies near Tulum in the Mexican state of Quintana Roo.
The cave passages are wholly or mostly filled with water.
By the beginning of 2026 over 540 kilometres of passages had been surveyed.
The caves formed in limestone, which is called karst.
Entrances to the caves are cenotes, natural water holes.

abschnitte.text: The **Yucatán** peninsula consists of **limestone**. Rainwater slowly dissolves this rock over a very long time. In this way passages and caves form underground. Such landscapes are called **karst**. Near Tulum a huge network of such passages has formed: the **Sistema Ox Bel Ha**. Today the passages are filled with water.

The passages are explored and surveyed by specially trained **cave divers**. They follow a guideline so that they can find the way back. By the beginning of 2026 over **540 kilometres** of underwater passages had been surveyed. This makes Ox Bel Ha the longest explored underwater cave system in the world. Cave diving is very dangerous and only for experts.

You reach the caves through **cenotes**. These are natural water holes that form when the roof of a cave collapses. For the **Maya** cenotes were important sources of water and holy places. In the caves there is often clear fresh water lying above heavier salt water from the sea.

gewusst: In the underwater caves of Yucatán the water is often so clear that divers can see many metres ahead.

teile.einleitung: The Sambadrome is a famous parade route in Rio de Janeiro. Here, at carnival, the great samba schools pass by with splendid costumes and floats. Tens of thousands of spectators sit in the stands.
wichtigste: The Sambadrome lies in Rio de Janeiro in Brazil.
It was opened in 1984.
The architect was Oscar Niemeyer.
The parade route is about 700 metres long.
At carnival the samba schools compete against one another here.

abschnitte.text: In the past the samba schools marched through ordinary streets of the city. Then in 1984 the **Sambadrome** was opened, a permanent parade route with stands on both sides. It was designed by the famous Brazilian architect **Oscar Niemeyer**. The route is about **700 metres** long. At the end lies a large square with a striking arch.

A **samba school** is not a school building but a club from a district of the city. All year round the members prepare their performance: music, dances, costumes and huge floats. At carnival each school passes through the Sambadrome for about an hour. A **jury** judges, for example, the music, costumes and floats. The best school becomes the winner of the carnival.

Outside carnival time concerts and other events also take place in the Sambadrome. At the **2016 Summer Olympic Games** in Rio the **archery** competitions were held here. In addition, the marathons started and finished there.

gewusst: A large samba school can march through the Sambadrome with several thousand dancers and musicians.
The parades often last the whole night until the morning.

teile.einleitung: The Selk'nam were an indigenous people who lived on the main island of Tierra del Fuego, right at the south of South America. They were hunters and lived mainly from hunting guanacos. They are also called the Ona.
wichtigste: The Selk'nam lived on the main island of Tierra del Fuego.
They are also called the Ona.
They hunted mainly guanacos, a kind of wild llama.
In the late 19th century they were almost wiped out through persecution and disease.
Today descendants of the Selk'nam live in Argentina and Chile.

abschnitte.titel: Life at the end of the world
abschnitte.text: **Tierra del Fuego** is a group of islands at the southern tip of South America. Today it belongs partly to **Argentina** and partly to **Chile**. On the large main island lived the **Selk'nam**, also called the **Ona**. The climate there is cool, windy and harsh. The Selk'nam moved through the land in groups and hunted mainly **guanacos** with bow and arrow. These are wild relatives of the llama. From their hides the Selk'nam made warm cloaks.

The Selk'nam had a rich culture with their own **stories** and **ceremonies**. At an important ceremony the men painted themselves with patterns and wore masks. In this way they represented spirits from their stories. The missionary and ethnologist **Martin Gusinde** visited the Selk'nam at the beginning of the 20th century and took photographs of this. These pictures are world famous today.

In the late 19th century many settlers came to Tierra del Fuego, also because of the **search for gold** and large **sheep farms**. The Selk'nam lost their land and were **persecuted**. In addition there were **diseases** that the immigrants brought in and against which the Selk'nam had no defences. Within a few decades they were almost wiped out. Today descendants are campaigning for their culture not to be forgotten.

gewusst: The photographs by Martin Gusinde of the painted Selk'nam are among the best-known pictures of Tierra del Fuego.

teile.einleitung: The Taj Mahal is a magnificent tomb of white marble in India. A ruler had it built for his late wife, and today it is regarded as one of the most beautiful buildings in the world.
wichtigste: The Taj Mahal stands in the city of Agra in India, on the River Yamuna.
The emperor Shah Jahan had it built as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
Shah Jahan was a ruler of the Mughal Empire.
The Taj Mahal is built of white marble.
Since 1983 it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and since 2007 one of the New 7 Wonders of the World.

abschnitte.text: The Taj Mahal is a **tomb**, a building for someone who has died. The ruler **Shah Jahan** had it built for his wife **Mumtaz Mahal**, who died in 1631. He wanted to set up a monument to her that would remind people of her for ever. Later Shah Jahan himself was also buried in the Taj Mahal, **next to his wife**.

Shah Jahan was an emperor of the **Mughal Empire**. From the 16th to the 18th century this empire ruled large parts of India. The Mughal rulers had magnificent palaces, gardens and mosques built. Building the Taj Mahal took many years, and thousands of craftsmen worked on it.

The Taj Mahal is built of **white marble**. Fine patterns of coloured **gemstones** are set into the stone. Depending on the time of day, the building shimmers white, pink or golden. In front of the tomb lies a large garden with water pools in which the building is reflected. It stands in **Agra** on the bank of the **River Yamuna**.

Around the tomb stand **four** slender towers, the **minarets**. They lean slightly outwards. This way, if they ever collapsed, for example in an earthquake, they would **not fall onto the tomb**. So the builders planned very far ahead.

Since **1983** the Taj Mahal has been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. In **2007** it was chosen in a worldwide vote as one of the **New 7 Wonders of the World**. Millions of people visit it every year. Because the air in Agra is polluted, the marble has to be cleaned again and again.

gewusst: The name Taj Mahal is often interpreted as “Crown of the Palace”.
The grave of Shah Jahan is the only part of the interior that is not arranged symmetrically.

teile.einleitung: A seaport is a port on the sea in which large ships dock, are loaded and unloaded. A large part of world trade passes through seaports. The largest ports in the world today lie in Asia.
wichtigste: The largest container port in the world is Shanghai.
Singapore also has one of the largest container ports.
Jebel Ali in Dubai is the largest port in the Middle East.
Hamburg has the largest seaport in Germany.
Antwerp in Belgium has the second largest port in Europe.
The largest container port in the USA is Los Angeles.

abschnitte.text: In a seaport ships dock at **quays**, that is, at reinforced shores. Huge **cranes** lift containers from the ships onto lorries or railway wagons. This process is called **handling**. Many goods travel in standardised **containers**, large steel boxes in fixed sizes. They are counted in **twenty-foot equivalent units** (TEU). Besides containers, oil, grain, ore and cars are also handled.

The port of **Shanghai** in China has been the largest **container port** in the world since 2010. It handles well over 40 million standard containers a year. The city state of **Singapore** also has one of the largest container ports. It lies conveniently on one of the most important **shipping routes** between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific. In the Middle East **Jebel Ali** in Dubai is the largest port. It was built artificially.

The largest port in Europe is **Rotterdam** in the Netherlands. The second largest is in **Antwerp** in Belgium, on the Scheldt. Since the merger with Zeebrugge it has been called **Antwerp-Bruges**. The **Port of Hamburg** is the largest in Germany. It lies on the **Elbe**, about 100 kilometres from the North Sea. In Greece the Chinese state shipping company **COSCO** took over the majority of the port of **Piraeus** near Athens in 2016. For China, Piraeus is an important gateway to Europe.

The largest container port in the **USA** is **Los Angeles** (as of 2024). It lies on the Pacific coast right next to the port of **Long Beach**. A large part of the trade with **Asia** passes through these two ports. From there the goods are distributed across the country by train and lorry.

Switzerland has no seaport. Goods from overseas mostly arrive through the large ports on the North Sea, such as Rotterdam or Antwerp. From there many goods travel on **Rhine ships** as far as the **Rhine ports** in Basel. These ports are Switzerland’s gateway to the sea. Other goods come by train or lorry from ports in Italy or France.

gewusst: A large container ship can today load over 20,000 standard containers.
In modern ports some container vehicles drive entirely without a driver.

teile.einleitung: A maritime climate is the climate near the sea. Mild winters and cool summers are typical. The sea acts like a huge store of heat that evens out the temperatures.
wichtigste: A maritime climate prevails on coasts and on islands.
The winters are mild, the summers rather cool.
The sea stores heat and evens out the temperatures.
It often rains, and the sky is frequently cloudy.
Examples are Ireland and Brittany.
The opposite is the continental climate with hot summers and cold winters.

abschnitte.titel: The sea as a heat store
abschnitte.text: Water warms up more slowly than land and also cools down more slowly. In summer the **sea** takes in a lot of heat, and in winter it gives it off again. That is why the differences between summer and winter on the coast are **small**. Experts also call a maritime climate an **oceanic climate**. The air is damp, and it rains spread across the whole year.

A typical maritime climate is found in **Ireland**, in Great Britain, in **Brittany** in France and on the coast of Norway. In Ireland it is rarely very cold in winter, and snow hardly lies. In return it rarely gets really hot in summer. Because it rains a lot, the meadows there grow especially green. Ireland is therefore also called the “Emerald Isle”.

Far from the sea, in the middle of large continents, the evening-out influence of the water is missing. There the **continental climate** prevails. The summers are hot, the winters very cold, and it rains less. An example is the interior of Russia. The further you go from the sea, the more **continental** the climate becomes.

Switzerland lies between these two climates. With the **westerly winds** damp air often comes from the **Atlantic**, bringing rain and mild temperatures. From the east, by contrast, dry air that is very cold in winter can arrive. That is why in Central Europe people speak of a **transitional climate**. In Switzerland there are also the influences of the **Alps**, which shape the weather strongly.

gewusst: The Gulf Stream brings warm water to northern Europe, which is why many ports in Norway do not freeze over in winter.
On some coasts in Ireland and south-west England palm trees even grow outdoors.

tqlqd8x.t: Rhaetian Railway in the Albula/Bernina Landscapes

teile.einleitung: The Albula line and the Bernina line of the Rhaetian Railway lead through the mountains of the Grisons as far as Italy. Because of their daring structures and the beautiful landscape, they have been part of the UNESCO World Heritage since 2008.
wichtigste: The World Heritage route runs from Thusis to Tirano in Italy.
Switzerland shares this World Heritage site with Italy.
The Landwasser Viaduct near Filisur leads straight into a tunnel in the rock face.
At the Brusio spiral viaduct the train passes in a circle under itself.
The highest point of the Bernina line is at the Ospizio Bernina at 2,253 m above sea level.
The Rhaetian Railway runs on metre gauge.
The Bernina Railway manages a gradient of 70 per mille without a rack.

abschnitte.text: The **Rhaetian Railway** is the big railway company in the canton of the **Grisons**. Two of its lines were included in the **UNESCO World Heritage** in 2008 together with the surrounding landscape: the **Albula line** and the **Bernina line**. The route leads from **Thusis** via St. Moritz to **Tirano** in Italy. That is why Switzerland shares this World Heritage site with **Italy**. The lines were built at the beginning of the 20th century.

The Albula line connects Thusis with the Engadine. Its most famous structure is the **Landwasser Viaduct** near **Filisur**. The tall stone bridge leads in a curve straight into a **tunnel** in the rock face. At **Bergün** the train has to climb a great deal of height over a short distance. To do this it goes through **spiral tunnels** and loops in which it turns inside the mountain. After that it goes through the **Albula Tunnel** into the Engadine.

The Bernina line leads from St. Moritz over the **Bernina Pass** down to Tirano. Its highest point is at the **Ospizio Bernina** at **2,253 m above sea level**. On the way you see glaciers and mountain lakes. The railway manages gradients of up to **70 per mille**, and does so entirely without a rack. That means: over 1,000 metres of track it climbs 70 metres. This makes it one of the steepest railways of this kind.

In the Val Poschiavo stands the **Brusio spiral viaduct**. Here the train runs on a bridge in a **circle** and passes under its own track. In this way it gains height in a tight space without becoming too steep. The Rhaetian Railway runs on **metre gauge**: the rails lie one metre apart. That is narrower than on most railways and allows tighter curves in the mountains.

gewusst: The Glacier Express and the Bernina Express also run over the World Heritage route.
The Bernina line is regarded as the highest railway connection across the Alps.

teile.einleitung: The Rocky Mountains are the largest mountain range in the west of North America. They stretch over thousands of kilometres from Canada to the south of the USA and are the home of many wild animals.
wichtigste: The Rocky Mountains lie in North America.
They are often called “the Rockies” for short.
The name simply means “rocky mountains”.
The range runs from north to south.
Grizzly bears, pumas, beavers and bighorn sheep live there.
In Canada, Banff National Park lies in the Rocky Mountains.
The bald eagle, the national bird of the USA, also lives there.

abschnitte.text: The **Rocky Mountains** lie in the west of **North America**. They run from **north to south**, from Canada to the US state of New Mexico. The range is several thousand kilometres long. The name simply means **“rocky mountains”**. People often say **“the Rockies”** for short. The highest peak is Mount Elbert in Colorado, which is over 4,000 metres high.

An important **watershed** runs through the Rocky Mountains. This is a line at which it is decided where the rainwater flows. On one side the rivers flow into the **Pacific**. On the other side they flow into the **Atlantic** or into the Gulf of Mexico. Many great rivers rise in the Rockies, for example the Rio Grande.

Many large animals live in the Rocky Mountains. The **grizzly bear** is a mighty brown bear. The **puma** is a large wild cat that is very shy. The **bighorn sheep** has big, curved horns and climbs skilfully on steep rocks. In the streams the **beaver** builds dams of wood. In the sky the **bald eagle**, the national bird of the USA, circles.

In the Rocky Mountains there are many **national parks**. In Canada lie **Banff** and Jasper, with turquoise lakes and glaciers. Banff is the oldest national park in Canada. In the USA there is Rocky Mountain National Park in Colorado. The famous **Yellowstone National Park** with its hot springs also lies in the area of the Rockies.

gewusst: Yellowstone National Park in the Rockies is regarded as the oldest national park in the world.
With their dams, beavers can turn whole valleys into ponds.

teile.einleitung: South America is a continent in the southern hemisphere and in the south of the double continent of America. It is known for the Andes, the Amazon and the largest rainforest on Earth.
wichtigste: South America lies south of North America and is connected to it through Central America.
In the west lies the Pacific, in the east the Atlantic.
The Andes are the longest mountain range on land.
The Amazon flows through the largest rainforest on Earth.
